title: X of a Kind in a Deck of Cards
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<int,int> count: up to n entries → O(n)
- gcd helper: iterative, no recursion → O(1)
- not counted: input vector
approach: Count the frequency of each distinct card value. We need a group size x > 1 that divides every frequency, so x must be a common divisor of all frequencies. The largest such x is the GCD of all frequencies; a valid partition exists if and only if that GCD is at least 2. We compute the GCD iteratively starting from 0 (since gcd(0, k) = k).
hints: If every group must contain exactly x cards of the same value, what relationship must x have with the count of each distinct value in the deck? The deck has at most 10^4 cards.
Compute the greatest common divisor (GCD) of all card frequencies. For Example 1, frequencies are {1:2, 2:2, 3:2, 4:2}; GCD(2,2,2,2) = 2 ≥ 2, so return true.

```
count = frequency of each distinct card value
g = 0
for each frequency f in count:
    g = gcd(g, f)
return g >= 2
```

**Single card** - only one card exists, no group of size > 1 is possible
`Input: [1]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking if all frequencies are equal (trivially true with one value) → returns true

**All same, odd prime count** - every card identical, count is an odd prime
`Input: [1,1,1]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: checking if all frequencies are even → returns false (3 is odd)

**Coprime frequencies** - two values whose counts share no common divisor > 1
`Input: [1,1,1,2,2]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking if all frequencies >= 2 → returns true (3 and 2 are both >= 2)

**Minimum valid partition** - exactly two of each value
`Input: [1,1,2,2]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using g > 2 instead of g >= 2 → returns false (GCD is 2, 2 > 2 is false)

followUps.q: What if card values are guaranteed to be in [0, 10^4)? Can you reduce space to O(1)?
followUps.a: Replace the hash map with a fixed-size array of 10^4 ints. Since 10^4 is a constant bound from the constraints, the auxiliary space becomes O(1). Time complexity stays O(n).

followUps.q: Instead of returning true/false, return the maximum possible group size x, or -1 if impossible.
followUps.a: The GCD of all frequencies is already the largest valid x. Return g if g >= 2, otherwise return -1. No change to time or space complexity.

followUps.q: What if groups can have different sizes, but each group size must be a prime number greater than 1?
followUps.a: For each frequency f, check if f can be expressed as a sum of primes > 1. Any f >= 2 works (f itself if prime, or 2 + (f-2) if f-2 is prime, or Goldbach decomposition for even f >= 4). This reduces to checking f >= 2 for each frequency. Time O(n), space O(n).
